{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABc8E4aw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGeLjo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 138, "title": "Fix rough PC-98 game audio using a rights-cleared music-capable guest and real browser playback validation", "body": "## Problem

A maintainer reports that **actual PC-98 DOS adventure-game music remains extremely rough/choppy** in the browser **after the structural Worker/AudioWorklet change in [Issue #136 / PR #137](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/137)**. The current `main` already has `web/emulator-worker.js` and `web/audio-worklet.js`, so repeating “move audio to a Worker” is not a solution. The user explicitly requests **finding and using a legally distributable/free PC-98 game with music to tune and validate the implementation**, rather than reasoning from source alone.

The underlying cause is **not established**. Possible distinct failure modes include guest execution/scheduling too slow to produce 48 kHz audio in real time; worklet underflow or overflow; lost/duplicated blocks; incorrect clock/tempo/IRQ behavior; and intrinsically approximate or missing YM2203/YM2608 FM/SSG/OPNA synthesis. Diagnose and correct the actual evidenced causes, not just suppress the symptoms.

### Relevant current implementation

- [`web/emulator-worker.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/emulator-worker.js): guest execution in fixed `core.step(10000)` slices; 48 kHz PCM copied in 1,024-sample transferable blocks with **six buffer credits**, then `core.audio_clear()`; finite queues may drop samples if production and consumption rates differ.
- [`web/audio-worklet.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/audio-worklet.js): fixed six-block queue, silent underflow, newest-block drop on overflow, 48 kHz source resampling to actual device rate, epoch flush and buffer recycling. Existing [`tests/audio-worklet.test.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tests/audio-worklet.test.js) tests basic order/underflow/overflow but **does not prove sustained real-game audio quality or absence of repeated underruns**.
- [`src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/lib.rs) and [`src/bus.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/bus.rs): deterministic guest 8 MHz model, eight clocks per instruction slot, audio generated from guest cycles; a CPU-heavy transition may slow guest audio generation relative to the browser output clock.
- [`src/sound.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/sound.rs): approximate mathematical OPN/OPNA FM and SSG synthesis, expensive per-operator sample math, limited envelope/timer/frequency fidelity. [`src/pcm.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/pcm.rs) provides the bounded 86 PCM subset. [`docs/ap-devices.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/ap-devices.md) documents missing rhythm samples, ADPCM, LFO, exact envelope/pan etc. Distinguish unsupported features from audio starvation.
- The repo already has an **MIT-licensed PC-98 DOS adventure game sample with PMD BGM**, `ADV98`, and independently built original MIT `PLAY.MML` music in [`fixtures/music-manifest.json`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/fixtures/music-manifest.json), [`fixtures/dos-apps-manifest.json`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/fixtures/dos-apps-manifest.json) and [`tools/prepare_music_fixture.py`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/tools/prepare_music_fixture.py). Existing smoke tests prove **nonzero audio and basic guest PMD execution**, not clean sustained BGM or scene-change behavior.

## Rights-cleared guest discovery is an explicit implementation deliverable

**Research, select, acquire, and document at least one genuine PC-98 DOS game or playable adventure sample with nontrivial FM/SSG BGM, legally usable in reproducible tests**. Start with the already independently audited candidate:

- [`yarufu/pc98` ADV98](https://github.com/yarufu/pc98), [official release](https://github.com/yarufu/pc98/releases): **MIT-licensed PC-98 adventure game/engine sample** with scenes, backgrounds, sprites, transitions, and PMD BGM support. This repo already pins its executable, source, FreeDOS environment and original MIT test score. It is the **preferred baseline candidate** if it exercises the symptom sufficiently.
- [`ADVS98`](https://delacannon.itch.io/advs98): a more recent MIT-described PC-98 adventure/visual-novel engine, with a 26K/86 sound-board distinction. **Candidate for discovery only**: inspect actual downloadable game/sample contents, full license terms for bundled art, music, DOS and PMD, source/binary availability, sound requirements and compatibility before using or redistributing. “Engine is MIT” does **not** establish that its included sample media are MIT.
- Broaden the search to other author-published PC-98 homebrew/freeware demos **only if** the above cannot provide an adequate independent musical game workload. “Free download”, abandonware, archive mirror, “freeware” and rights to play **do not automatically grant redistribution/CI/publication rights**. Distinguish original author's permission from third-party soundtracks/assets and proprietary DOS/ROM. Do not use another emulator's source or copy/translate its sound implementation.

Record **URLs, exact version/commit, file-level license evidence for executable + soundtrack + art + drivers, SHA-256 checksums, allowed use, and source/notice requirements** in an auditable fixture manifest. Pin downloads; avoid fetching mutable latest artifacts. Prefer the already legal ADV98+original-score fixture over spending time searching indefinitely. If no independently distributable new game meets requirements, use the existing MIT ADV98 with original MIT score and record the candidate evaluation; **lack of an additional game must not prevent fixing verified audio defects**.

The guest must actually run through **the real FreeDOS(98) and emulated PC-98 sound hardware**, not play a pre-rendered WAV/MP3 or a host-side synth. Keep legal test disk images in ignored local fixture directories; publish only assets with verified publication rights and approved site-audit updates, if truly necessary. No private commercial/adult game HDI, audio recording or ROM/font dump in repo, CI, Pages or PR artifacts.

## Expected outcome

**Correct noticeably rough/choppy music in sustained, real, music-capable PC-98 DOS guest gameplay** while preserving guest time, FM/SSG pitch/tempo, IRQ ordering and deterministic emulation. The result should be demonstrated through an **automated real-Wasm browser playback scenario**, not only unit tests or `audioEnergy > 0`.

Do not assume that “audio is rough” is caused only by CPU overload: discriminate **delivery underflow/overflow** from **wrong FM/SSG synthesis/timing** and from **intentional unsupported instrument/OPNA features**. Prefer coherent fixes in worker pacing, bounded PCM queue/scheduling, audio producer/sink protocol, or the original OPN synthesis as warranted. Avoid adding latency indefinitely, stretching tempo to hide slow emulation, silent sample duplication, or game-specific shortcuts.

## Investigation and implementation

1. **Acquire and run the licensed guest.** First reproduce sustained BGM with the pinned ADV98+PMD+original score on the current production release-Wasm Chromium runtime, including transitions with bitmap/CG updates and HDD/DOS I/O if supported. Confirm the guest is genuinely playing FM/SSG by real port writes, timer IRQ and PCM output. If inadequate, identify, license-audit, pin and build a second freely redistributable musical PC-98 DOS game/demo with actual interactive graphics/scene transitions.
2. **Use focused, lightweight diagnostics** (not a broad performance-profiling project): collect bounded Worker-produced sample counts, Worklet consumed sample counts, underflows/overflows, queue occupancy, flush epochs, real-time guest advancement, FM register/key-edge and relevant IRQ events around an actual scene change. Compare with a stable musical segment and with mute/resume/reset. Observe whether missing audio comes from the producer, message delivery, sink or missing chip feature. Do not collect/upload the user's private game, or require subjective manual listening as a pre-merge gate.
3. **Fix the identified systemic problems** in the correct layer. Evaluate Worker tick pacing and yielding, 10,000-instruction batch cadence, 8 MHz guest virtual clock, PCM credit recycling, AudioWorklet 128-frame callbacks, queue capacity/backpressure, sample-rate conversion and underrun recovery. If synthesis fidelity is the problem, correct original FM/SSG envelope/pitch/algorithm/timer/IRQ math with independent Yamaha datasheet references and tests. If a real guest uses unsupported OPNA rhythm/ADPCM, specify the necessary bounded, legally implementable subset; do not invent copyrighted sample ROMs or hide missing sounds with fabricated tones.
4. **Validate audio continuity and correctness** across long BGM playback and scene changes. Use deterministic source-side expected PCM/counters and browser sink-side consumed-sample order, finite queue and underflow/overflow accounting. Assertions should detect a concrete audible class of defect (sustained starvation, dropped/reordered samples, wrong tempo/pitch, persistent silence, stuck sound after pause/reset), not merely assert that some energy is nonzero. When physical browser/audio hardware limitations prevent guaranteeing zero glitches, document a realistic bounded behavior and show meaningful improvement on the same fixture.
5. **Keep correctness and scope:** preserve UI responsiveness, Worker single-owner semantics, 640x400 display, FreeDOS desktop/HimemX, IDE/FDD import/export, pause/mute/visibility, sound enable gesture, audio epoch flushing, 26K vs 86/OPNA profile behavior, VM compatibility, reset and audio device sample rates (44.1/48/96 kHz where relevant). Avoid an unlimited audio buffer, double-running guest, full-HDD cloning, new cross-origin isolation requirement, third-party emulator code, or proprietary media.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document a **specific chosen PC-98 music-capable game/sample** and how to reproduce real DOS gameplay/music in the test environment. Include independent evidence for the executable, all music and image assets, PMD/driver and DOS licenses, pinned source URLs/versions/hashes, notices, and whether redistribution in local CI and/or public Pages is allowed. **Existing MIT ADV98 + original MIT score is an acceptable selection if adequate**; explicitly evaluate at least one alternative or justify why no additional guest is needed.
- [ ] Add or extend a rights-cleared **actual guest** fixture/scenario that plays sustained music through the emulator's OPN/OPNA ports **while rendering/transitioning scenes**, with stable deterministic setup and no copyrighted commercial game data. Keep fixture download/build time bounded and preserve existing checksums unless deliberately updating a manifest.
- [ ] Reproduce and distinguish **PCM producer shortfall, queue starvation/overflow, resampling or clock error, and unsupported synthesis** using small bounded diagnostic observations from the real Worker/AudioWorklet. Record the evidenced root cause(s) in PR/validation notes; no mandatory comprehensive baseline profiling or FPS study.
- [ ] Implement a substantive, general fix supported by the observed reproduction. The same legal guest must pass an automated regression detecting the original symptom in production release-Wasm Chromium: sustained sample flow, correct order, finite latency/queue, sensible guest time/pitch, and no persistent dropouts across a scene transition. A static “audioEnergy > 0” assertion is insufficient; don't pass by playing a fake prerecorded audio track.
- [ ] Test pause/resume, mute/unmute, reset, visibility suspension, sample-rate conversion, underflow/overflow recovery, audio worklet credit recycling and no stale epoch playback; maintain responsive DOM input during guest scene transitions.
- [ ] Verify representative FM/SSG timer/IRQ/PMD and 86 PCM behavior with original native Rust and real browser tests, preserve previously accepted OPNA channel-3 behavior, and keep VM beeper unaffected. If any missing hardware feature remains, state precisely which legal guest instrument/function requires it and do not claim all PC-98 music is supported.
- [ ] Run relevant native/fixture/license checks, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, release Wasm build and full applicable real-Wasm Chromium suite at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Apply [development-flow CI performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles): avoid redundant huge HDI exports, repeated media downloads and gratuitous browser combinations.
- [ ] English Issue/PR/review/commit text; original independent Rust/JS implementation. No private media or proprietary NEC BIOS/ROM/font dumps; no code copied/ported from an existing emulator. No user-specific game, physical hardware, manual listening, post-merge Pages check or other human action as a pre-merge gate.

## Optional validation

The maintainer may privately compare the same legally held adventure game's BGM before/after the fix and report whether the subjective roughness improves, without disclosing media or raw audio. An optional locally generated synthetic/reference PCM clip may help characterize FM timbre; it cannot substitute for actual guest PMD music.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Deployment-only issues should be separate `task` Issues.
